pillar_reactions.evidence: Rep delivered the full pillar — strength, conditioning and mobility in one session, 30-40 minutes, three to four times a week, plus separate five-to-ten-minute mobility protocols. Asked 'Do you have any questions on that? How do you feel about the structure of this?' and got 'Okay, that's all good.' The prospect had already primed himself for it: 'I grabbed a kettle ball, and I did something... And man, I hit muscles that I wasn't hitting. And I was like, this is cool.' Time efficiency landed as the hook — he agreed he only wants to 'do so many exercises and try to, and get out'.

Understood and agreed with the what/when/how-much structure, and asked a series of mechanics questions rather than pushing back: 'How do I begin the diet? How does that begin?' and 'is it diet the same for everybody, or is he...' He also tested the rep on fermentation detail — 'What is it? Fermented or double fermented? do you know?' — which the rep deflected. No objection to the substance; the eight-hour window was already his habit.

Delivered in full (weekly in-app check-in, video form review, Trevor's personal cell number, over-communication). Reaction was polite but flat and immediately redirected to price: 'No, that's good. I just keep, I'm waiting for what it's going to cost.' He later probed how real the human contact was — 'how personable is it? ... is it just all app, you know, or is there a real, is he really' — which the rep answered with the Zoom onboarding and video feedback.

anchors.raw: That's what I was thinking. I was thinking that, if was me, what would I want? What would I charge?
anchors.note: The rep floated the number as 'You were thinking 6K' and the prospect confirmed he had independently arrived at $6,000 by pricing it as a business owner would. The price was fully accepted before any discounting began — which makes the subsequent collapse to a $1,200 one-month tier a pure margin giveaway rather than a concession that saved a deal.

anchors.raw: my payroll is $20,000 every two weeks
anchors.note: Alongside 'people wire us $50,000, man, like that, you know, I mean, for a watch' and 'I got the cash.' Affordability was never in question; the rep discounted against a buyer who had explicitly stated he can pay and refuses financing on principle.

anchors.raw: I just got a whole panel done at Quest, and big one, like 78 deals, tests
anchors.note: Pays out of pocket for annual Lifeline screenings and full Quest panels, follows supplement brands, has done genetic testing. Established habit of paying for health information — a supportive anchor the rep never leveraged.

unmet_demand.want: Protection against paying six months up front and the single coach becoming unavailable — 'I don't want to pay out the six grand and then he dies or something.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme is built around one named coach, Trevor, and the rep had no continuity, refund or escrow answer. He responded with payment terms instead. The performance guarantee that might have addressed the risk was not surfaced until the prospect read it aloud from the agreement document forty minutes later, well after the deal had already been reduced to one month.

unmet_demand.want: Guidance on supervised extended fasting as an active protocol, having asked about starting a three-to-four-day fast that day
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep stopped him doing it alone and promised Trevor would 'design the whole fasting protocol for you', including 24, 36, 48 and 72-hour fasts. Whether a coaching programme should be prescribing multi-day fasts to a 64-year-old with a total cholesterol of 328 and no clinician involved is unresolved, and nothing in the offer describes clinical oversight.
